blockers: Frozen criterion 6 remains unmet: independent design validation failed, no independent harness was frozen, and no baseline/candidate acceptance or deliberate-regression rejection result exists. Full acceptance remains unmet.

findings.description: The experiment cannot be accepted. Project regression success does not establish the required independent coverage, baseline compatibility, or mutation sensitivity.
findings.evidence: bundle.json records tester_failure.artifact_check.valid=false with reason 'Design/harness mismatch'; independent_acceptance.status='NOT RUN', frozen_design=false and frozen_harness=false. Rejected artifacts were not preserved.

findings.description: The refactoring has genuine engineering value: pure outcome preparation separates interpretation from database effects, and one small executor removes duplicated successful-record persistence. Responsibilities and transaction ordering are easier to inspect and preparation is directly testable without a database. The abstraction remains Steam Store-specific and adds only standard-library dependencies.
findings.evidence: src/transform.py:331-395 contains effect-free preparation; src/load.py:585-602 centralizes the formerly duplicated connection/cursor/load_transformed_record sequence. Existing adapter signatures remain at src/load.py:605 and :617.

findings.description: Static comparison found no concrete regression in the specified input branches: outcome lookup, falsy-appid early return, invalid-ok fallback, native transformer exceptions, exact diagnostics and ordinary-only truncation remain consistent. This supports compatibility but does not complete independent acceptance.
findings.evidence: candidate.patch preserves the original branch conditions and error strings in the preparation functions. src/transform.py:374-380 returns before redirect transformation for falsy appids; :392 slices ordinary diagnostics only. The original parser and game transformer remain unchanged.

findings.description: The executor preserves target persistence before the separate requested-row mark, including rollback suppression and partial success on mark failure. Body identity and redirect pointer remain separate; file marks retain fetched_at and is_replay=True. Added PostgreSQL tests meaningfully exercise counters, replay, rollback and committed-target behavior, but are implementer tests.
findings.evidence: src/load.py:588-600 exits the metadata connection context before marking, without an added commit. src/transform.py:358-367 keeps the transformed body record separate from appid and redirect_to. tests/test_refactoring.py includes real-database failure and replay assertions.

findings.description: The preparation boundary still couples transform to the marking function's keyword schema through dict[str, Any] and ** expansion. The frozen dataclass does not freeze its dictionaries, so misspelled fields or later mutation can produce runtime failures. Positional redirect-plan construction also requires reading the field declaration to understand its values. These are maintainability limitations, not demonstrated behavioral defects.
findings.evidence: src/transform.py:321-328 defines mutable dictionary fields; :361-368 constructs the redirect plan positionally. src/load.py:600 forwards the dictionary directly to mark_steam_store_enrichment_result.

findings.description: Controller evidence supports exact candidate reproduction, unchanged persistence/components and passing project checks. It cannot substitute for independent acceptance.
findings.evidence: bundle.json reports candidate_reproduced_exactly=true, patch_applies_to_fixed_source=true, 210 project tests with zero failures/errors/skips, final implementer unit/integration/lint success, and unchanged_components.persistence_sql_unchanged=true.

rationale: Reject the experiment because frozen criterion 6 and full acceptance remain unmet. The refactoring itself provides genuine, proportionate engineering value, and static review found no blocking code defect in the specified behavior. Its dictionary-based internal contract is a nonblocking maintenance concern. Controller checks and implementer tests provide useful evidence, but no independent acceptance result exists.
